transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Kim (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Solstice - Head of ML Ops), Ethan Park (Solstice - Dir Eng), Priya Nair (Solstice - Cloud Architect)

Summary:
Quick renewal / expansion check-in. Customer is approaching renewal and is evaluating capacity upgrade (additional dedicated GPU pool), expansion into APAC regions, and possible term extension for better unit pricing. Discussed technical constraints (VPC peering, KMS, SOC2), benchmark plan, and next steps.

Topics (auto): renewal options, dedicated capacity sizing, APAC deployment, compliance & logs, pricing/unit economics, pilot/benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey team, hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I'm Avery from Redwood, with Samir, our SE, and Jules our CSM.
[00:12] Marta: Hi, Marta here. Ethan and Priya are with me.
[00:16] Ethan: Hey all.
[00:18] Priya: Morning.
[00:20] Avery: Cool, agenda today — renewal timing, capacity needs for Q4, APAC region support, and any compliance questions. We also want to confirm next steps for a bench.
[00:31] Marta: Sounds good. We're on a 12-month contract that ends mid-September and we've seen steady growth in inference traffic, mainly recommendation and search rerank. We're looking at dedicated capacity because the transient latency on shared was starting to hurt conversion during peak.
[00:46] Samir: Right, last time we recommended the dedicated pool — I think you were on a 2x g5 equivalent reserved pool? I have notes that your 95th p95 latency target is 200 ms for the short queries, and that was slipping to 300–350 during promo spikes.
[01:06] Marta: Yeah, exactly. The baseline was fine but spikes are the problem. Also want APAC region — we have storefronts in Singapore and Sydney, and the round trip plus routing to us in us-east was adding 80–120 ms.
[01:21] Priya: From infra side, two things: VPC peering and KMS. We need a private deployment or VPC option. We prefer customer-managed KMS for keys and want to know audit log retention. Also curious about on-prem option if there's a cardholder data scope issue.
[01:36] Jules: We'll share the SOC 2 + ISO docs and our audit log retention policies. Redwood's Private/VPC offering supports customer KMS and can be deployed in a customer's VPC or via our private package — Samir can go into tech details.
[01:50] Samir: Quick clarification: our 'Redwood Dedicated' offering (transcript says "Redwood Dedicate" a couple times) gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput. For APAC we can spin up a dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1 — same runtime, same model pinning, and we support multi-region routing with automatic fallback to the US pool if capacity is saturated. That said, the KV cache warm-up across regions is an obvious factor for cold queries.
[02:16] Ethan: On fallback — if ap-southeast is overloaded, what's the added latency and is there a way to prefer cheaper/faster models for low-priority traffic?
[02:24] Samir: Fallback adds round trip to US plus the model inference time; typical extra 150–250 ms depending on region. You can define routing policies by route: prefer lowest latency, or prefer cost, and set fallbacks to smaller quantized variants. We'll show an example config.
[02:40] Marta: Pricing — we want a committed discount if we commit to a 24-month term and add the APAC pool. Can you share SKU-level pricing?
[02:48] Avery: Sure — we can provide 12/24/36 month options. We typically give better unit pricing at 24 months and a bigger uplift for 36. I'll send a SKU price sheet and examples of unit economics at the levels you're looking at.
[02:58] Priya: Also need to understand network peering charges — will we pay egress to Redwood or is that included in the dedicated contract?
[03:05] Jules: We'll include a section in the doc about egress. In dedicated/private setups there's usually interconnect cost; we'll map it out with region-specific estimates.
[03:15] Ethan: For benchmarks, we want a throughput run on the APAC pool mirroring our workload — 30 tpm for rerank, 5k tokens/session average. Can you run that or we run it ourselves?
[03:26] Samir: We can run it on a Redwood dev pool but prefer to run it on a mirrored dedicated pool to avoid discrepancy. Proposal: spin up a 2x g5-dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1 for 72 hours and run your harness — we'll collaborate on the test harness and metrics.
[03:42] Marta: That works, timeline wise we need results ahead of renewal decision — ideally first week of September.
[03:49] Samir: We can start the pool by next week; I'll need the exact seed prompts and traffic pattern.
[03:55] Priya: We'll share traffic pattern and anonymized payloads — need to confirm no PHI or card data.
[04:01] Samir: Good call. If you have PCI scope concerns, we should check the private on-prem option. But often the VPC + customer KMS path reduces scope sufficiently.
[04:12] Ethan: Question on SLA — if we move to dedicated can we get a latency SLO for 99th percentile? Our SREs want an SLO in writing.
[04:19] Avery: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency goals in the enterprise pack. We can include a 99th p99 latency target for your traffic profile in the contract, with remediation steps if violated. I'll get legal to include an appendix.
[04:33] Marta: Excellent. Also, one more procurement note — our procurement asked if Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning users.
[04:40] Jules: Yes, SAML + SCIM supported; we'll attach the SSO integration guide.
[04:45] Priya: For KMS — we need HSM-backed keys in our KMS. Is that compatible?
[04:50] Samir: Yes, customer-managed KMS using HSM-backed keys is supported; we integrate with major cloud KMS providers and bring-your-own-key workflows. For on-prem, we also support external HSM via standard connectors.
[04:59] Ethan: About model versions — we pin to a specific open model, we want a rollback policy if a new model causes regressions. How do rollouts work?
[05:07] Samir: Rollouts — canary, A/B, and auto-fallback to pinned version. We also have quality monitoring tied to your prompt sets; if regression detected we'll auto-rollback or route traffic away.
[05:18] Marta: Nice. Any points you're worried about from Redwood side?
[05:21] Avery: Mostly just aligning on APAC capacity and pricing. Also making sure we have the benchmarks and compliance docs in time for procurement.
[05:27] Ethan: Timeline recap — we need pricing and contract options by 2027-08-27, benchmark results by 2027-09-01, and final decision by 2027-09-08 (before current term lapses).
[05:36] Avery: That's doable. We'll follow up with the price sheet and a proposed statement of work.
[05:40] Marta: Cool. Couple of small transcribe glitches from our end — I think Samir said "KV cache" but the transcript has a few mis-hearings, it's fine.
[05:49] Samir: Yeah sometimes the auto transcript flips words.
[05:52] Jules: I'll add a notes doc summarizing the call and upload the SOC2/ISO pack.
[05:57] Priya: One more question — are there any hidden costs with multi-region routing? Specifically storage for cache replication?
[06:04] Samir: Cache is primarily warmed per region; we don't replicate full KV across regions by default. There is storage for persistent caches and that will be in the pricing sheet as a small line item. We'll call it out.
[06:16] Ethan: For the benchmark, Samir, can you include tail-latency breakdown and token-cost analysis?
[06:21] Samir: Yep, we'll include p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost at the tested batch sizes.
[06:26] Marta: Okay, I think that's most of it. Can we do a short recap of next steps?
[06:30] Avery: Recap: Avery sends SKU/pricing and term options by 2027-08-27; Samir to provision APAC dedicated pool and run benchmark w/ Solstice harness by 2027-09-01; Jules to send compliance docs and SSO guide by 2027-08-26; Priya to confirm region list and any data residency constraints by 2027-08-30.
[06:50] Priya: Sounds good.
[06:52] Marta: Thanks everyone.
[06:54] Avery: Thanks — we'll follow up in an email with links to the docs and the benchmark plan.

Auto sections (optional):
Action items (auto): See above.
Questions:
- Will dedicated pool in APAC cover peak promos consistently? (Samir to answer via benchmark)
- Is on-prem required for PCI scope? (Priya to decide after compliance docs)

Shared artifacts mentioned:
- SKU/pricing spreadsheet (to be sent)
- SOC 2 / ISO + audit logs guide (Jules to attach)
- Benchmark harness (Solstice to share anonymized traffic)
- Example routing policy and rollback playbook (Samir to share link)

Call end: 15:45 UTC

Recap (final):
Customer is highly likely to renew and expand into a dedicated APAC pool if pricing and benchmarks meet expectations. Redwood to provide clear pricing, SLA appendix, and run a short dedicated throughput test. Procurement and compliance gating items identified (KMS/HSM, SAML/SCIM, audit log retention).
